questions.def: Third conditional: 'would have + past participle' expresses unreal past.
questions.question: If I had known, I ___ you.

questions.def: Future perfect expresses completion before a future point.
questions.question: By the time you arrive, I ___ the report.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: action started in the past, continues now.
questions.question: He ___ here since he graduated.

questions.def: Mixed conditional (past unreal condition, past unreal result).
questions.question: I ___ to the gym if it hadn't rained.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous emphasizes duration of an action.
questions.question: She ___ the piano since she was five.

questions.def: Third conditional: 'If + past perfect, would have + past participle'.
questions.question: If he ___ harder, he would have passed.

questions.def: 'Wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past.
questions.question: I wish I ___ harder in school.

questions.def: Simple past for completed action in the past.
questions.question: He ___ to London last year and loved it.

questions.def: 'Is knowing' should be 'has known' since 'know' is stative.
questions.question: She is knowing him since they met last year.

questions.def: Past perfect indicates action completed before another past action.
questions.question: They ___ here before moving to Rome.

questions.def: Reported speech: 'will' changes to 'would' after past tense 'said'.
questions.question: She said she ___ me later.

questions.def: 'If only' + past perfect expresses regret about the past.
questions.question: If only I ___ more attention in class!

questions.def: Present perfect continuous: action started in past and continues.
questions.question: We ___ for the bus for an hour.

questions.def: Future perfect: action will be completed before a future time.
questions.question: By next year, I ___ my degree.

questions.def: Past continuous: action in progress when another action interrupted.
questions.question: He ___ when the phone rang.

questions.def: Third conditional: 'If + past perfect, would have + past participle'.
questions.question: If I ___, I would have helped.

questions.def: Past perfect to show an action before another action in the past.
questions.question: She ___ in Paris before moving here.

questions.def: Third conditional: unreal past condition, unreal past result.
questions.question: I ___ to the concert if I hadn't been busy.

questions.def: 'Is working' should be 'has been working' with 'since'.
questions.question: He is working here since last summer, hasn't he?

questions.def: 'Wish' + past perfect to express regret about past feeling.
questions.question: I wish I ___ better yesterday.

questions.def: Future perfect: action completed before another future action.
questions.question: By the time he calls, I ___.

questions.def: Mixed conditional: past unreal condition, present unreal result.
questions.question: If she ___ harder, she would pass now.

questions.def: 'Are knowing' incorrect; use 'have known' with stative verb.
questions.question: They are knowing the truth since they have investigated.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous to show duration before another past action.
questions.question: She ___ in Italy before moving to Spain.

questions.def: Reported speech: 'is' changes to 'was' after past tense 'said'.
questions.question: She said she ___ coming to the party.

questions.def: Future perfect continuous: duration up to a future point.
questions.question: I ___ here for ten years by next July.

questions.def: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.question: If I had known, I ___ you.

questions.def: Past perfect shows an action completed before another in the past.
questions.question: By the time she arrived, they ___ all the food.

questions.def: Reported speech: 'will' changes to 'would' after a past reporting verb.
questions.question: He said he will call me later.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for actions started in past and continuing now.
questions.question: She ___ here since she graduated.
